title: On Changing the plan at the last minute
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：change　|　正文 365 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 change 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1960 the clerk ① changed the plan at the last minute without a word of thanks, and every applicant in the office said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three months on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the clerk ② changes the plan at the last minute at once without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ change the plan at the last minute at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ changed the plan at the last minute before — a line in the file for May 1954 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Changing the plan at the last minute without a word of thanks, the clerk said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the stamp at the far counter, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ change the note at the village shop at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Change the note at the village shop at once and never mention it again.

By 1967 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the file, and a new applicant from the next office ⑧ changes the note at the village shop without a word of thanks every month without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the counter, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ changed the plan at the last minute again when nobody else would.

⑩ To change the plan at the last minute, my mother said in 1972, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the office remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the office forgets, somebody changes the plan at the last minute at once again and somebody must change the plan at the last minute without a word of thanks all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 改变（一般过去式 changed the plan at the last minute：1960 年书记员头一回这样做，不图一句谢）
B. v. 改变（一般现在 changes the plan at the last minute：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 改变（不定式 to change the plan at the last minute：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 改变（过去完成时 had changed the plan at the last minute：1954 年五月的卷宗上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 改变（动名词 changing the plan at the last minute 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 更换（change the note at the village shop：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去更换在小铺把零钱换开）
G. v. 更换（change the note at the village shop：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 改变（后段两处：新来的申请人照例 changes the note at the village shop，而母亲又一次 changed the plan at the last minute）

answers.why: change 意为“改变”，1960 年书记员不图一句谢改变最后一刻改了主意，那是办事处里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 changed。
change 意为“改变”，自那以后书记员二话不说地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 changes。
change 意为“改变”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯改变最后一刻改了主意”，此处为不定式 to change the plan at the last minute。
change 意为“改变”，卷宗里 五月 那行字说明早在 1967 年之前就有人改变过，故用过去完成时 had changed。
change 意为“改变”，书记员说“改变最后一刻改了主意这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 changing the plan at the last minute 作主语。
change 意为“更换”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去更换在小铺把零钱换开”，should ever 之后用原形 change the note at the village shop。
change 意为“更换”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻更换在小铺把零钱换开（change the note at the village shop at once），以后再也不要提起。
change 意为“改变”，新来的申请人每个月份都照例更换在小铺把零钱换开，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 changes。
change 意为“改变”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次不图一句谢改变最后一刻改了主意，用一般过去式 changed 叙述。
change 意为“改变”，结尾那句是母亲 1972 年的话：要改变最后一刻改了主意，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和办事处记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 change 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1960 the clerk changed the plan at the last minute without a word of thanks, and nobody in the office forgot it.
Even now the clerk changes the plan at the last minute at once whenever the office asks.
Changing the plan at the last minute without a word of thanks, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever change the note at the village shop at once, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new applicant from the next office changes the note at the village shop without a word of thanks every month, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother changed the plan at the last minute again, and the office remembered that half.
